::: {.scope-note}
**What this covers.** Five files were accepted by Evalbase: three Retrieval runs
and two Retrieval-Augmented Generation runs. This explains the one retrieval run
they all come from, the point where the two tasks stop sharing anything, and the
checks each file passed on the way out. Everything here is aggregate provenance
that is already checked into the repository — no test narrative, passage, prompt,
provider response, or generated answer.
:::

[Open the project artifact hub](../index.html) or go straight to the
[submission ledger](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/SUBMISSION_LEDGER.md).

One thing is worth saying before anything else, because it is the shape of the
whole system and it is easy to assume otherwise: **The Retrieval TSV is not
Generation input.** We froze a single retrieval run. One branch replays it to
rank documents. A separate branch hands sealed evidence to the answer writers.
Neither branch opens the other's output.

### How to read every image {.unnumbered}

The nine diagrams share one grammar, so colour and shape mean the same thing in
all of them.

- Teal is source and submission Retrieval. Indigo is RAG Generation.
- Amber is advisory model work, or a bounded control decision.
- Solid arrows carry data or evidence. Dashed arrows carry advisory, fallback,
  or validation control.
- Folded documents are durable artifacts. Cylinders are stores. Diamonds are
  validation gates.
- Counts name their unit. Documents, chunks, passages, selected evidence, and
  advisory hints are different things and are never added together.

# Frozen source, two submission branches {#whole-system}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** One retrieval run is the fork in the road. What comes out of it are
two sibling submissions, not a pipeline that runs Retrieval first and feeds RAG
second.
:::

![One source retrieval run, two sibling submission branches.](2026-competition-architecture/01-whole-system.svg){#fig-whole-system fig-alt="An official narrative enters bounded source retrieval and produces the authenticated facet-deepseek-b40-v3 source. One branch creates a robust variable-depth candidate core and three Retrieval TSVs. A separate sealed selected-evidence handoff feeds single-pass and multi-stage RAG, producing two JSONLs. All five files pass local validation and are accepted by Evalbase."}

[Open the reusable whole-system SVG](2026-competition-architecture/01-whole-system.svg){.figure-source}

The frozen source is called `facet-deepseek-b40-v3`. It holds what one retrieval
run produced: the plan, the BM25 results, the neural passage scores, the passages
we selected, and the claim hints generated beside them. Nothing was added to it
afterwards.

From there the two branches do different work. The Retrieval branch reopens only
the authenticated lanes and the cached scores, and uses them to decide which
documents each narrative should rank and in what order. The RAG branch takes a
separate, purpose-built handoff of selected evidence and never opens a finished
Retrieval run at all.

They diverge because the two tasks ask different questions. Retrieval asks which
ClimbMix documents deserve to be ranked as useful evidence. RAG asks for a cited
answer from a system that has already done its own retrieval. Sharing a source
does not make one organizer file the other's runtime input.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The final artifact map and exact hashes live in the
  [submission ledger](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/SUBMISSION_LEDGER.md).
- The Retrieval branch is documented in its
  [bundle architecture](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/retrieval/cache-first-candidate-core-v1/ARCHITECTURE.md).
- The RAG branch is documented in its
  [bundle README](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/rag/selected-evidence-sol-v1/README.md).
- The source identifier is provenance, not a public link. Its contents stay out
  of this report.

</details>

# The search widens once, then stops {#source-retrieval}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** The source run widens the search a single time, puts every query
through the same ceilings, and freezes the passages it selected before either
branch touches them.
:::

![Every query lane crosses the same ceilings before the source freezes.](2026-competition-architecture/02-frozen-source-retrieval.svg){#fig-source-retrieval fig-alt="The untouched narrative and bounded DeepSeek subnarratives create query lanes. Every lane searches the climbmix-400b BM25 index through Pyserini, chunks returned documents, scores passages with the Mixedbread cross-encoder, selects exact evidence, and creates advisory hints before the source artifact is frozen."}

[Open the reusable source-retrieval SVG](2026-competition-architecture/02-frozen-source-retrieval.svg){.figure-source}

An official narrative is long — a paragraph of situation followed by several
questions — and it is almost never one search. So the narrative itself always
gets a lane, untouched, and one call to
`deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-20260423` may add up to eight focused
subnarratives, each carrying one to three BM25 queries. That caps a topic at 25
searches including the original lane. There is no loop back from results to
planning.

Each query may pull at most 1,000 documents from the Pyserini REST
`climbmix-400b` index. A document is not a unit a reranker can score, so
documents become overlapping chunks of `3500 characters` with `350-character
overlap`. The pinned `mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-base-v2` cross-encoder scores
each query–passage pair, and the run keeps at most 100 passages per focused
query before local selection narrows them further. A one-shot Nuggetizer stage
then writes advisory claim hints beside the evidence. Selected passages are
factual authority. Canonical claim hints are advisory: they suggest what an
answer should cover and are never citable themselves.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The source configuration is
  [`configs/rag26_competition_retrieval_v2.yaml`](../configs/rag26_competition_retrieval_v2.yaml).
- Planning is implemented in
  [`facet_extraction.py`](../code/trec_rag/facet_extraction.py); source
  orchestration is in
  [`competition_retrieval.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_retrieval.py).
- Passage scoring uses the pinned model revision recorded in the final
  Retrieval bundle metadata.
- The 1,000-document and 100-passage values are per-query internal ceilings, and
  the unit changes from documents to passages between them. Neither is the final
  submission depth.

</details>

# Planning stays one-shot {#planning}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** DeepSeek V4 Flash may widen the search. It cannot start a second
round, and it cannot remove the original narrative.
:::

![One planner call, with no path from results back to planning.](2026-competition-architecture/03-bounded-deepseek-planning.svg){#fig-planning fig-alt="One DeepSeek V4 Flash request receives the complete narrative. The original lane remains. Zero to eight subnarratives may each propose one to three BM25 queries. Schema or semantic failure falls back to the original lane, and no retrieved result returns to the planner."}

[Open the reusable bounded-planning SVG](2026-competition-architecture/03-bounded-deepseek-planning.svg){.figure-source}

The planner's job is breadth: break a long information need into search-shaped
pieces. It is good at that and it is not an authority on anything. The code owns
the limits, keeps the original narrative whatever the planner returns, validates
the structured plan, and falls back to the original lane alone when the plan does
not parse or does not make sense.

For the Retrieval replay, each authenticated `facet:<subnarrative>:text` lane
counts as one pooled source. We do not treat the individual planned query strings
as separate pools after the fact, because the frozen artifact did not keep their
results apart. The replay only claims what the provenance can support.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The bounded planning and fallback contract is enforced by
  [`facet_extraction.py`](../code/trec_rag/facet_extraction.py) and
  [`competition_retrieval.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_retrieval.py).
- The final source and pooled-lane interpretation are recorded in the
  [Retrieval architecture](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/retrieval/cache-first-candidate-core-v1/ARCHITECTURE.md).
- No qrels, gold nuggets, or RAGDoll results participate in planning or replay.

</details>

# How deep each Retrieval run goes {#candidate-core}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Depth comes from the evidence, not from a round number. Each lane
admits its own outliers, the union becomes the candidate core, and nothing is
padded to reach a cutoff.
:::

![Each lane admits its own outliers; their union sets the depth.](2026-competition-architecture/04-variable-depth-candidate-core.svg){#fig-candidate-core fig-alt="Each authenticated source lane computes its median aggregate score and median absolute deviation. Documents above the robust lane threshold are admitted. The original and all subnarrative admissions form an inclusive union. An empty union would retain the best original-lane document. The observed final depth ranges from one to 121 documents."}

[Open the reusable candidate-core SVG](2026-competition-architecture/04-variable-depth-candidate-core.svg){.figure-source}

A fixed depth of 100 would be a guess about every narrative at once. Instead each
lane asks which of its own documents stand out from its own distribution. For
lane (u), with (A_u(d)) a document's finite aggregate score, (m_u) the lane
median, and (mathrm{MAD}_u) the median absolute deviation, a document is admitted
when:

```text
MAD > 0: A(d) >= median + 2.5 × 1.4826 × MAD
MAD = 0: A(d) > median
```

The candidate core is the inclusive union of what the original lane admitted and
what every subnarrative lane admitted. Had a union come back empty, the strongest
original-lane document would have survived on deterministic retrieval-rank and
UTF-8 document-ID tie breaks. No topic needed that.

Across 119 narratives the core holds 4,246 topic–document pairs. Its variable
depth runs from **1–121 documents**, across 61 distinct values of (k). All three
Retrieval runs share one core per narrative.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The exact admission formula, fallback, and observed counts are preserved in
  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/retrieval/cache-first-candidate-core-v1/ARCHITECTURE.md).
- [`retrieval_candidate_core.py`](../code/trec_rag/retrieval_candidate_core.py)
  implements robust candidate admission.
- Final per-topic cutoff receipts are authenticated in
  [`retrieval-baseline-runs-manifest.json`](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/retrieval/cache-first-candidate-core-v1/retrieval-baseline-runs-manifest.json).

</details>

# Three orderings, one candidate set {#retrieval-runs}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** The three Retrieval runs change the order of the same documents and
nothing else, which is what makes comparing them mean anything.
:::

![One scored matrix, three orderings over identical document sets.](2026-competition-architecture/05-targeted-scoring-and-runs.svg){#fig-retrieval-runs fig-alt="The shared candidate core is chunked and scored against the untouched narrative and every subnarrative. Cached Mixedbread scores complete one targeted matrix. Percentiles feed three orderings: narrative plus subnarrative, evidence breadth, and narrative only. All three emit the same narrative-specific document sets."}

[Open the reusable targeted-scoring SVG](2026-competition-architecture/05-targeted-scoring-and-runs.svg){.figure-source}

Every candidate document is scored against the untouched narrative and against
every subnarrative. Overlapping passage scores are suppressed, then the best four
retained passages are weighted 0.55, 0.25, 0.13, and 0.07 and turned into tied
percentiles within each narrative and semantic unit. The replay needed 167,597
cached query–passage scores and ran no model batches at all: zero cache misses.

The three accepted orderings are:

1. **Narrative + subnarrative — `r26-narr-facet-v1`.** A 50/50 blend of the
   narrative percentile and a facet score built from the best two subnarrative
   percentiles (0.7 best + 0.3 second-best).
2. **Evidence breadth — `r26-facet-breadth-v1`.** Lexicographic ordering by
   supported subnarrative count, strong passage count, combo score, source rank,
   and document ID.
3. **Narrative only — `r26-narrative-v1`.** Narrative percentile, then source
   rank, then document ID.

Each file has 4,246 rows. Within a narrative the three files list exactly the
same documents; only the ranking moves.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- [`retrieval_baseline_runs.py`](../code/trec_rag/retrieval_baseline_runs.py)

- The [Retrieval bundle README](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/retrieval/cache-first-candidate-core-v1/README.md)
  records the accepted files and validation counts.
- [`metadata.json`](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/retrieval/cache-first-candidate-core-v1/metadata.json)

</details>

# What Generation is allowed to see {#handoff}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** The handoff is the trust boundary. Generation authenticates it and
can open nothing else — not the sibling Retrieval files, not evaluation material.
:::

![What the handoff carries, and the five artifacts it bars.](2026-competition-architecture/06-generation-handoff-contract.svg){#fig-handoff fig-alt="The sealed generation handoff contains the exact narrative, 691 evidence groups across 119 topics, selected passages, advisory hints, allowed ClimbMix citation IDs, source receipts, and hashes. Single-pass and multi-stage generation authenticate it. The Retrieval TSV, full-text ZIP, qrels, gold nuggets, and RAGDoll scores are barred."}

[Open the reusable handoff-contract SVG](2026-competition-architecture/06-generation-handoff-contract.svg){.figure-source}

`generation_handoff_manifest.json` and its topic payloads carry 119 topics and
691 evidence groups. Each topic binds its exact narrative, the selected passages,
the advisory claim hints, the allowed citation domain, and the source receipts,
all through canonical serialization and hashes. Anything malformed,
contradictory, non-canonical, or unauthenticated fails the load rather than
degrading quietly.

Five things are barred from Generation, and it is worth naming them: the accepted
Retrieval TSV, the source full-text ZIP, qrels, gold nuggets, and RAGDoll scores.
The first two are the sibling branch's own output. The last three are evaluation
or gold material, and a system that reads them is no longer answering the
question the track asked.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- [`generation_handoff.py`](../code/trec_rag/generation_handoff.py) defines
  canonical serialization, payload hashes, context hashes, and validation.
- The RAG bundle records handoff manifest SHA-256
  `31dc1b3578741339101b8199c0ea027e2d8405e828532aa58f86bf74c0542a0d`.
- The handoff itself is private and is deliberately not copied into this report
  or the submission bundle.

</details>

# Single-pass RAG {#single-pass}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Sol sees all of the authenticated evidence at once, writes one
structured answer, and gets at most one more attempt if local validation rejects
it.
:::

![Sol writes once; local validation decides whether it ships.](2026-competition-architecture/07-single-pass-rag.svg){#fig-single-pass fig-alt="The authenticated handoff becomes one deterministic selected-evidence prompt for GPT-5.6 Sol. Sol uses medium reasoning, strict structured output, and a 12,000-token ceiling. Local validation checks exact narrative metadata, the allowed citation domain, reference uniqueness, exact-hint citations, and the 1,024-word ceiling before publishing rag26-ss1."}

[Open the reusable single-pass SVG](2026-competition-architecture/07-single-pass-rag.svg){.figure-source}

This is the simpler of the two strategies, and it is the one to understand first.
`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` runs with medium reasoning, strict structured output, no
explicit temperature, a **12,000-token ceiling**, and four topics in flight at a
time. The handoff is rendered deterministically into one prompt, and Sol returns
organizer-shaped answer objects citing raw allowed ClimbMix document IDs.

Then local code checks the result: the exact topic and narrative, the required
metadata, the answer structure, unique references, the allowed citation domain,
the exact-hint citation rules, and the **1,024-word ceiling**. Two of 119 topics
needed the configured second attempt. The accepted `rag26-ss1` file took 121 Sol
calls and cost $52.14302500 as reported by the provider. Its answers run from 203
to 749 words with 10 to 40 references.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- [`competition_rag.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag.py) implements
  request rendering, transport retry, semantic validation, resume identity,
  and atomic publication.
- [`configs/rag26_competition_rag_gpt_sol_v2.yaml`](../configs/rag26_competition_rag_gpt_sol_v2.yaml)
  preserves the checked-in model and request shape.
- Aggregate production counts and cost are in the RAG bundle
  [`metadata.json`](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/rag/selected-evidence-sol-v1/metadata.json).

</details>

# Multi-stage RAG {#multi-stage}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** A second model spends bounded effort on coverage and on whether an
edit is safe. If any of that work fails, the validated draft is what ships.
:::

![Luna plans and screens, Sol writes, local code applies only what passed.](2026-competition-architecture/08-multistage-rag.svg){#fig-multi-stage fig-alt="Luna creates a narrative blueprint and audits each authenticated evidence group. Sol writes a structured draft, then may propose a bounded splice revision. Luna screens proposed operations for support, atomicity, materiality, redundancy, and replacement safety. Local code applies only accepted operations; malformed or rejected work preserves the validated draft. Final validation publishes rag26-ms1-final."}

[Open the reusable multi-stage SVG](2026-competition-architecture/08-multistage-rag.svg){.figure-source}

The same sealed evidence goes to two models instead of one.
`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` writes a compact narrative blueprint, audits each
authenticated evidence group once, and optionally screens proposed edits.
`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` writes the draft and may propose one bounded splice
revision. The normal ceiling is two Sol reservations, draft and revision, with a
third allowed only to repair a deterministic validation failure.

Every boundary belongs to local code, not to either model. The blueprint has to
anchor its obligations to the narrative and to authenticated evidence. Revision
operations are indexed against the immutable draft and have to fit hard
insertion, replacement, citation, and word budgets. Luna's screen asks five
questions of each operation — support, atomicity, materiality, redundancy,
replacement safety — and only the operations that pass are applied. Anything
malformed, ambiguous, or unsafe leaves the already validated draft standing.

The accepted `rag26-ms1-final` run made 894 Luna calls and 264 Sol calls, 1,158
provider calls in all, at a provider-reported cost of $50.423054730. Six planner
responses needed deterministic deadline normalization and strict revalidation.
There were no final failures and no operation-screen crash fallbacks. Answers run
from 531 to 1,011 words with 14 to 136 references.

<details><summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- [`competition_rag_multistage.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag_multistage.py)
  provides full-run identity, bounded concurrency, resume, failure recording,
  final-row reload, and all-or-nothing publication.
- [`narrative_blueprint.py`](../code/trec_rag/narrative_blueprint.py),
  [`bounded_splice.py`](../code/trec_rag/bounded_splice.py), and
  [`operation_screen.py`](../code/trec_rag/operation_screen.py) define the
  bounded stage contracts.
- The final run statistics and warnings are preserved in the RAG bundle
  [`metadata.json`](../submissions/trec-rag-2026/rag/selected-evidence-sol-v1/metadata.json).

</details>

# Final analysis reports {#final-analysis-reports}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Three analyses exist. None of them is an official score, and none of
them changed what we submitted.
:::

There is one tracked 119-topic Retrieval quality analysis, and two separate
119-topic RAGDoll citation-support reports, one per accepted RAG run. RAGDoll
measures citation support, not official TREC correctness: it asks whether a
statement is backed by the passage it points at. qrel/gold metrics are
unavailable. The evaluation did not influence accepted priority — the accepted
files and their recorded priorities are unchanged.

# Sources, validation, and scope {#sources}

This report is a reader-facing synthesis of the accepted bundle documentation,
the machine-readable metadata, the reusable implementation, the checked-in
configs, and the pinned official contracts linked above. The canonical authored
source is
[`reports/2026-competition-architecture.qmd`](2026-competition-architecture.qmd);
the standalone HTML is generated from it with Quarto 1.9.38. The diagrams and
their source map live in
[`reports/2026-competition-architecture/`](2026-competition-architecture/README.md).

Verified here: the architecture boundaries, the aggregate source and submission
counts, the model and call identities recorded in checked-in metadata, the
organizer-format validation, the exact accepted-file hashes, and which artifact
belongs to which branch.

Not claimed here: official effectiveness scores, that any of the five runs beats
another, or fresh validation of the private handoff that is not in this
repository. Acceptance means the files were delivered in valid form. It says
nothing about how good they are.

The project is finished. The historical specifications and experiment reports are
provenance worth keeping, not a list of work still to do.
